notes: Virtual receiver only. Speeds, stopping and tracking values are rehearsal settings, not measured physical behavior.

Gains are the legacy collector's full tuned values (hold_kp at max_kp); unqualified for the guarded controller. The collector's 0.3 first-motion kp scale was used first and was too weak on the real arm: commands were then position-only, so a joint's drive was hold_kp times its lead, and at 0.3 J2 and J3 (3.2 and 1.9 Nm at the lead limit) could not lift the arm, J1 followed at about 0.11 rad/s, and the wrists stalled on friction (J5 2.4 Nm/rad held 0.063 rad off target by 0.15 Nm). The operator chose the full gains on 2026-09-27: more force on contact (J2 17.6 Nm before its tracking bound), with collision checks still advisory.
J6 holds at 8 Nm/rad, above the collector's 3: at 3 its drive at the lead limit (0.14 Nm) did not break its friction, and it did not move in the first live sessions.

Each leader channel's hand-swept range (Helm Leaders tab) scales straight onto its robot joint's whole usable range. Arm joints scale from the operator-set leader zero (mapped onto the robot's reference pose) with one scale for both directions, sized so both robot ends are reached; past a robot limit the leader goes on and the robot holds.

Grippers touch and hold objects: no margin, no stopping reserve, no braking (a stop keeps the last target) and no tracking-error fault; effort and gain limits still bound them. They run at 10 rad/s over their whole range.

Control law (2026-09-28): the receiver ramps each command over interpolation_ms, one loop period (20 ms: the loop runs at 50 Hz since 2026-10-04, 25 Hz before), from where the previous one pointed, with the command's velocity fed forward, and a joint with a saved servo sweep also gets 70% of its measured friction fed forward in the direction of motion. J2-J4 (parallel horizontal axes) also get gravity fed forward at the commanded pose, from each joint's gravity slice measured by its sweep (control/gravity.py; the servo calibration's gravity section), so the position loop no longer holds the arm up and J2/J3 can lift through their whole swept range. Before this, commands were position-only: a servo lagged by hold_kd * speed / hold_kp, so its own damping braked every motion (J2 at 1.5 rad/s: 22 Nm, 0.1 rad of lag) and the lead cap throttled it. A command still leads its measured position by at most 60% of the joint's tracking bound (a lead at the whole bound faulted J4 on a quick leader motion in the first live session).

Speed caps: J1-J3 1.5 rad/s, J4 2.5, the wrists (J5, J6) 4. Near an end every joint slows on the receiver's braking curve (it stops at its stop_acceleration after the 40 ms limit reaction), so a cap costs no travel. The wrist swivels (J5) map about 1.2-2 rad of leader travel onto about 4.6 rad. A servo calibration made under the old position-only law keeps its gains, braking and tracking bound but not its speed (guarded_config.CONTROL_LAW); a new sweep measures the speed under this law.

Range: an arm joint's operational range is its hand-swept range (Helm Limits) plus 0.02 rad of overtravel before the receiver faults (control/approach.py OVERTRAVEL_RAD); the CAD's nominal limits and the old 0.05 rad margin no longer narrow it. Its targets stay only its approach floor's stopping margin (about 0.03 rad) inside that.

An arm route sign says whether the leader angle and the robot's CAD joint angle increase together; a gripper route sign of +1 means the leader angle increasing opens the gripper. Signs are candidates until verified in Helm.

Collision checks are advisory: the conservative keep-out bound only certifies about +/-0.011 rad per arm joint at the hanging pose (about 0.03 rad/s). Each cycle is still checked and shown in Helm; the virtual receiver is not blocked. Physical teleop needs a tighter, still-sound bound and enforced checks.

live.note: Live teleop drives one arm on its physical motors, with advisory collision checks, the other arm never enabled; or both arms from one receiver, with the two-arm (motion) collision bound enforced (2026-10-05). Each session starts from the reference pose (arms straight down, grippers closed). The motion settings below are unqualified: attended tests only, with the foot switch in reach.

sweep.note: The servo sweep (Helm's Tune tab, control/servo_sweep.py) steps each joint's stiffness from kp_ceiling down (default: its current hold gain), damping ratios, then speeds up to its speed cap (speed_ceiling raises a joint's cap for the sweep, at the cost of usable range: the receiver's collision reserve is taken at the cap). Defaults are in servo_sweep.DEFAULTS. The wrists get headroom: friction held J5 and J6 off target at their collector gains, and the first J6 sweep (2026-09-27) passed only its top rung, 16, so the wrists go to 24. bound_ceiling and speed_ceiling let the sweep set a joint's tracking bound and speed cap from its measurements (never lowered, and only while its usable range stays at least usable_floor of its swept travel): the light distal joints only (operator's choice, 2026-09-27); J1-J3 keep their bounds; speed costs no travel (braking curves), so the sweep may test J1-J3 up to 1.5 rad/s (operator's choice, 2026-09-27) and J4-J6 up to their caps. Grippers are not swept (operator's choice, 2026-10-09: they squeeze what they hold); Minerva Check's live sweep opens each from its swept min to its swept max and closes it.
